cross_channel: At LifeSpan Fitness, I balanced DTC, Amazon, and B2B/retail channels, including Costco and Dick’s Sporting Goods. DTC generated the strongest returns, followed by Amazon and B2B, while higher-volume B2B sales helped sustain cash flow when e-commerce softened. I recommended allocating investment around channel profitability, inventory, warehouse capacity, available capital, and website and advertising needs rather than optimizing each channel in isolation.
cross_functional: At GRIP6, I worked closely with video, design, and writing teams to explain the benefits of wool socks and underwear to audiences who associated wool with discomfort. I aligned creative and content around product education and a try-and-buy program, giving the team a shared message and a practical path from discovery to product trial.
traffic_quality: In an e-commerce campaign, strong website traffic was not translating into sufficient sales. I used heatmaps and CRO analysis to identify friction, reviewed pricing and customer feedback, refined product specifications, and introduced promotions. This shifted the focus from click volume to conversion barriers and helped increase product sales.
local_campaigns: For a business operating eight construction companies, I managed local marketing through Google Local Services Ads, Google Business Profile, Yelp, Angi, KSL, and other lead sources. I tailored Utah campaigns by service area, travel time, demographics, equipment availability, and scheduling capacity, using CRM history and customer lifetime value to prioritize attractive markets.
qbr: I would lead a home-services QBR with qualified leads, booked jobs, customer acquisition cost, revenue, and customer value, then explain performance by service, market, and channel. I would connect results to sales conversion and operational capacity rather than lead volume alone. If results missed goals, I would acknowledge the gap, identify the drivers, and propose a focused plan with owners, budgets, and measurable next-quarter targets.
lead_quality: At Any Hour Services, I helped connect lead quality to roughly 32 marketing channels, including Google Ads, door hangers, fridge magnets, and referrals. We used AI analysis of inbound calls to assess lead quality alongside acquisition-source information. At TravelPass Group, I worked on a similar process that used lead-quality scores to prioritize calls and route stronger prospects to the appropriate teams. This connected marketing measurement to qualification and handoff rather than volume alone.
mmm: I built Python models relating marketing-channel spend to sales and revenue and led geographic, audience, and multivariate incrementality testing. We kept roughly 70% of our market and customers on established campaigns as a comparison baseline, then applied successful test findings to the broader program. I presented results to marketing leadership weekly; I also do this in my current role, at a smaller scale.
